cases.title: Requests, responses, headers, and forms
cases.rationale: Public value semantics are replayed unchanged against upstream Scrapy and both SpiderOxide engines.

cases.title: Request serialization and fingerprints
cases.rationale: Public serialization, curl rendering, canonicalization, and fingerprint outputs are compared byte-for-byte.

cases.title: Settings and priorities
cases.rationale: Priority resolution, typed getters, copying, and project-facing settings behavior are compared directly.

cases.title: Selectors, items, loaders, and links
cases.rationale: Representative public extraction, link normalization, item, and loader results are compared structurally.

cases.title: Spider helpers, sitemap parsing, and utilities
cases.rationale: Documented spider and utility outputs are compared without depending on Scrapy private implementation state.

cases.title: Crawler, runner, process, and spider-loader APIs
cases.rationale: Public constructor and method signatures are compared, while lifecycle behavior is exercised by the real-crawl case. SpiderOxide's additive keyword-only downloader injection hook is normalized out.

cases.title: Real crawl lifecycle
cases.rationale: The same data-URI spider runs through upstream Scrapy and SpiderOxide's Python and Rust engines.

cases.title: Implemented middleware, pipelines, exporters, queues, and extensions
cases.rationale: These public behaviors already have repository verification scripts, but their upstream pytest fixtures are private to Scrapy. Differential probes will replace the local adaptations incrementally.

cases.title: Private engine, scraper, downloader, and protocol internals
cases.rationale: These modules assert undocumented Scrapy and Twisted implementation details rather than public compatibility contracts.

cases.title: Upstream test infrastructure and dependency checks
cases.rationale: These tests validate Scrapy's own test fixtures, dependency declarations, resource cleanup helpers, or test server rather than application behavior.

cases.title: CLI commands and project generators
cases.rationale: Command metadata is compared directly with Scrapy 2.19, while subprocess integration covers dispatch, generated projects, crawls, feed output, and inspection commands.

cases.title: Add-ons and runtime services
cases.rationale: Scrapy add-on ordering, settings mutation, factories, opt-outs, and inspection are compared directly; SpiderOxide service lifecycle behavior is exercised on both engines.

cases.title: Spider contracts
cases.rationale: Contract discovery, request construction, callback arguments, return and item validation are compared directly; subprocess integration covers custom contracts, async callbacks, reporting, and exit codes.

cases.title: Resolvers, TLS, HTTP/2, and low-level networking configuration
cases.rationale: Resolver and TLS context compatibility is tracked by issue #46.

cases.title: Logging, mail, console, template, and remaining utilities
cases.rationale: Remaining public exceptions, logging, mail, and utility APIs are tracked by issue #47.

cases.title: Telnet, remote control, throttling, and mail-based extensions
cases.rationale: Remote-control and remaining extension interfaces are tracked by issue #48.

cases.title: Third-party integration behavior
cases.rationale: Third-party Scrapy integration certification is tracked by issue #49.

cases.title: Deferred, reactor, signal, and subprocess integration
cases.rationale: Twisted Deferred and reactor compatibility is tracked by issue #50; SpiderOxide's asyncio behavior is covered separately.

cases.title: Version aliases and deprecation behavior
cases.rationale: Version and deprecation compatibility is tracked by issue #52.
